hook.text: A channel holds stones between two walls.

lines.text: A channel holds stones between two walls.
A channel setting holds a row of stones between metal walls.
The jeweler cuts a small seat inside the walls.
Each stone's edge, the girdle, rests in its seat.
Then the walls are pressed over the stones to lock them.
Stones must match in size and height, or gaps show.
No prongs means less snagging, and the surface sits flush.
It is hard to resize, and harder to repair than prongs.
Walls block some side light, and dirt can collect in the groove.
So a channel holds stones with walls instead of prongs.
A render shows how the row sits before anything is cast.

post.caption: A channel setting holds a row of stones between two walls of metal instead of prongs. The jeweler cuts a seat inside the walls, each stone rests in it by its girdle, and the walls are pressed over the stones to lock them in. Stones must match in size and height, and the setting is hard to resize and harder to repair than prongs. The renders in this video were made with HeyGema.
